chunks: And they will say to their skins, 'Why did you testify against us?' They will answer, 'God gave articulation to us, He who gave articulation to every thing, and He created you the first time; and to Him you will be returned.'

key_terms.أَنْطَقَنَا: He gave us the power of articulation/speech

ai.seo_question: Why will human skin testify against them on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the concept of *tadbir al-qudrah* (divine management of power), where the skin testifies not by its own volition but as an instrument of God’s will, emphasizing human accountability for their own choices. The reference to God who 'gave speech to every thing' underscores the transition from potentiality to actuality in creation, serving as a reminder that the same Creator who initiated existence will reclaim it. This scene illustrates the inevitability of divine justice, where the physical self becomes the primary witness against the soul's negligence.
